name: Vienna
title: Holidays in Vienna
intro: A giant Ferris wheel, the world's oldest zoo and cake in grand cafés. Here's what Vienna is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are warm and green, with outdoor swimming on the Danube. From mid-November the city is full of Christmas markets. January and February are cold but quiet.

things.name: Prater
things.blurb: A funfair park with the famous Giant Ferris Wheel. Entry is free and you pay per ride.

things.name: Schönbrunn Zoo
things.blurb: The world's oldest zoo, in the grounds of a palace, with pandas and polar bears.

things.name: Natural History Museum
things.blurb: Dinosaurs, meteorites and a huge collection of stuffed animals.

things.name: Haus der Musik
things.blurb: Conduct a virtual orchestra and play with sound.

things.name: Danube Island
things.blurb: A long island for cycling, picnics and swimming in summer.

things.name: Spanish Riding School
things.blurb: Watch the white Lipizzaner horses at their morning training.

faqs.question: Is Vienna good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's clean, safe and easy to get around, with parks and museums for all ages. Children under six ride public transport free.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three or four nights covers the city at a gentle pace.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Is Vienna expensive?
faqs.answer: About the same as a big UK city. Many parks and the Prater are free, and lunch menus are good value.
